plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $31, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $31, ensuring I maximize expected profit without risk of overpaying.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since I don't win by bidding above value (I'd overpay) and don't gain by bidding below value (I might lose profitable opportunities), I should bid exactly my value of $46. This ensures I win whenever profitable and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks overpaying, and bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding at $35 maximizes my expected profit.
